Container.Name: pingkit-agent
Container.Overview: PingKit Agent watches your own network from your Unraid server, which stays on, and sends PingKit on your iPhone an alert when the internet goes down (about three minutes) and comes back, when a new device joins, and, if you turn it on, when a device goes offline (up to 45 minutes at the default sweep). Pair it with the code your iPhone shows under Agents, Add an Agent. iPhone alerts need PingKit Guardian. The status page is on port 7474. Host networking is the one privilege: it lets the agent read the neighbour (ARP) table and hear mDNS and SSDP. To keep the state in appdata instead of the Docker volume, create /mnt/user/appdata/pingkit-agent owned by 65532:65532 (chown 65532:65532 in the Unraid terminal) and replace the --mount option in Extra Parameters with -v /mnt/user/appdata/pingkit-agent:/data. Without ping permission on the host (net.ipv4.ping_group_range), the agent uses ARP and TCP checks.
Container.Requires: A Linux host network. PingKit on an iPhone to pair it.

Config.Name: Claim code
Config.Description: The 8-character code your iPhone shows under Agents, Add an Agent. It works once and expires 10 minutes after your iPhone shows it, though it stays visible in the container settings; clear it after pairing, or type it on the status page instead.

Config.Name: Status page port
Config.Description: The status page (HTTP). With host networking the agent listens on this port directly; change PINGKIT_PORT to move it.

Config.Name: iPhone connection port
Config.Description: The HTTPS port your iPhone connects to the agent on. Change PINGKIT_API_PORT to move it.

Config.Name: Interface
Config.Description: The interface to watch, for example br0. Empty: the default route's interface.
